header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-02 11:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Ryan Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Brooks (Redwood CSM); Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI Head of Infra), Tom Bauer (SpectralAI ML Platform Eng), Priya Singh (SpectralAI CTO)
Shared assets: redwood_optimize_playbook_v3.pdf (link shared), spectral-traffic-sample.csv (customer), cost-model-sandbox.xlsx (to be sent)
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on batching + prefix/KV cache recommendations and a proposed cache-handoff pattern for SpectralAI's multi-tenant real-time assistant. We ran through a cost model with sample traffic, discussed tradeoffs of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and agreed next steps for a 24-hour dedicated benchmark and security docs. Customer signaled interest but has questions about KMS integration and cross-region cache warming.
topics: Batch size and batching policy (adaptive vs fixed)
Prefix/KV cache strategy and cache-handoff between sessions
Cost model assumptions: tokens/request, RPS, token price
Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Security: KMS, SOC2, audit logs, VPC peering
transcript:
00:00:03 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Ryan, AE on the Optimize team, with Maya our SE. We'll run through a playbook for caching and batching and then map it onto your traffic. Um, feel free to interrupt.
00:00:12 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): Hey Ryan, thanks. We're excited, we shared the traffic sample and we really want to see where we can get cost down without blowing up P95.
00:00:20 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Great. Quick agenda: 1) Quick context/gather requirements, 2) demo of Optimize console - batching and cache configs, 3) cost model with your numbers, 4) cache-handoff pattern sketch and risks.
00:00:35 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): One ask up front — we need to keep sub-150ms tail for our critical flows, and any caching can't add inconsistent staleness.
00:00:45 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Perfect, we'll call that out. Also, quick qual — are you planning to run this on Hosted first or do you have Dedicated reserved capacity in mind?
00:00:55 Priya Singh (SpectralAI CTO): Ideally Dedicated, but we need the security runbook for Private/VPC before we can commit. SOC two is required for procurement.
00:01:06 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Noted. We have an enterprise pack for Private with KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. I'll drop the diagram after.
00:01:15 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Ok jumping into the console — I'm going to share the Optimize savings sandbox. Bear with the screen share.
00:01:32 Speaker 1: [screen share noise]
00:01:42 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): So here's the workloads pane. We can import your CSV sample — I see a lot of short-context sessions and a long tail of occasional heavy sessions. That's where batching and prefix cache can help.
00:02:06 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): Quick clarification — when you say prefix cache, you mean the KV prefix cache / session prefetch? We call it lookahead in our infra so sometimes names different.
00:02:14 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Yeah sorry, names vary. Prefix/KV cache here is the ability to cache repeated initial prompts or persona prefixes and rehydrate KV so decoding cost drops. Lookahead == prefetch in some docs.
:00:02:36 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Good question — we recommend tenant-scoped cache keys. In Private/Dedicated you can scope to tenant-id + model-id. No data leakage; keys are hashed and stored in isolated namespaces when you choose dedicated pools.
00:02:48 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Also, for Hosted we do logical isolation and encryption at rest, but you said SOC2 is a blocker for procurement so probably Dedicated or Private for you.
00:02:58 Priya Singh (SpectralAI CTO): Yeah procurement won't sign off without SOC2 + KMS.
00:03:04 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Noted. Back to batching: we demo two policies — adaptive batching that increases batch size when queue depth is high, and fixed micro-batching optimized for sub-90ms median. Adaptive yields more token-cost savings for bursty traffic.
00:03:25 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): Show numbers? Our RPS is 80 steady and spikes to 400 for 10 minutes during peak.
00:03:33 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Pulling that into the cost model. With your steady 80 RPS and average prompt 60 tokens, baseline token cost (no caching, no batching) at our hosted tier is approx $0.00045 per token* — using placeholder, we'll refine per contract. With adaptive batching + KV prefretching you can see token-per-response drop by ~28% in the model.
00:04:05 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): 28% is great but where does cache-handoff come in?
00:04:12 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Cache-handoff is a pattern we sketched — when a user moves between sessions or context windows, you precompute and handoff KV entries between models or workers. Example: User opens chat in web, you prefetch their profile prefix KV and attach to subsequent mobile requests, reducing repeated prefix decoding.
00:04:34 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): That needs sticky keys — session affinity? We have autoscaling clusters that may not preserve local memory.
00:04:41 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Exactly — we recommend either a centralized fast KV store (in-memory redis with TTLs) or route affinity to keep KV cache warm in GPU local memory for ultra-low latency paths. Tradeoff: centralized KV adds network hop but simpler handoff; local GPU cache is fastest but needs smart routing.
00:05:02 Priya Singh (SpectralAI CTO): Network hop could blow P95. Our P95 can't exceed 150ms.
00:05:07 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Understood. In our simulations, centralized Redis adds ~6–12ms median, but can add tail variance under load. Local cache with smart routing kept P95 under 120ms in our benchmark, but requires Dedicated pools with session affinity.
00:05:27 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): I'll flag that to the pilot scope: test both modes.
00:05:33 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): Can you run the pilot on Dedicated during our peak window? We want to see cold-start to warm cache effects.
00:05:41 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Yes — propose a 24-hour dedicated run that covers a peak window. We'll set up traffic mirroring from your production sample.
00:05:49 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): About token quantization/optimized kernels — do you recommend quantizing our models or using a smaller variant for low-cost fallbacks?
00:05:58 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Two levers: quantization inside the GPU reduces per-token cost but sometimes slightly changes output quality. The usual pattern: primary model quantized to int8 for cost, fallback to full-precision or alternative open model on errors. For safety-critical flows keep a quality guardrail.
00:06:18 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): How do we measure quality regressions? We need automatic evals.
00:06:22 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Optimize ties into the evals pipeline — you can register prompt sets and get regression alerts when latency or outputs diverge past thresholds. We'll help configure your standard prompt set.
00:06:33 Priya Singh (SpectralAI CTO): Ok, show me the console cost simulator with our numbers.
00:06:39 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Switching to the simulator. I'm inputting: steady RPS 80, spike to 400 for 10 minutes, avg prompt 60 tokens, avg response 140 tokens, 30% repeatable prefix rate.
00:06:57 Speaker 2: [typing]
00:07:08 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Baseline monthly estimate (no caching/no batching) = $12,400 (placeholder). With prefix caching + adaptive batching the model projects $8,900 — about 28% savings. If you add cache-handoff and session affinity we get another 6–9% in peak efficiency because fewer cold decodes.
00:07:30 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): Those absolute numbers are helpful. What assumptions for token price did you use?
00:07:36 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Used per-token $0.00045 for generation; embedding/kv cost negligible per op but network/redis ops counted as $Y in infra cost — we'll replace placeholders with your procurement rates.
00:07:49 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): Can you annotate sensitivity — e.g., what if avg response tokens go to 260 instead of 140?
00:07:56 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Sure. Doubling response length increases token cost linearly; savings from batching still compress per-token overhead but prefix cache helps less proportionally. I'll add sensitivity rows in the sheet.
00:08:09 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Quick pause — security Qs?
00:08:14 Priya Singh (SpectralAI CTO): KMS integration — we need customer-managed keys and rotation. Also audit logs for cache reads/writes because certain prefixes can include PII in our use case.
00:08:24 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): For Private and Dedicated we support KMS integration and can log cache read/write events to your audit pipeline. Keys never leave your HSM in Private deployment.
00:08:33 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI ML Platform Eng): What about TTLs and eviction policies? We have short-lived session tokens that must expire quickly.
00:08:40 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): We recommend TTLs aligned with session lifetimes; for sensitive tokens use ephemeral keys and shorter TTLs, e.g., 5–15 minutes. Eviction: LRU for redis, and priority pinned for hot prefixes. We'll show the TTL tuning guide.
00:08:57 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): I'm going to sketch the pilot plan: 24-hour dedicated run, two cache modes (central Redis vs local GPU affinity), instrumented with token-level traces and cost breakdown. We'll run canary traffic first then full mirroring.
00:09:12 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): How much engineering effort to wire up the telemetry? Our infra team is lean.
00:09:18 Liam Brooks (Redwood CSM): We usually provide instrumentation helpers and a small integration guide; SE time estimated 2–3 days for the pilot wiring, plus one day for smoke. We'll staff that with Maya.
00:09:29 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): Timeline for pricing? We need quotes for Dedicated capacity.
00:09:34 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): I'll send an initial quote range in the next two business days. Final depends on committed throughput.
00:09:40 Priya Singh (SpectralAI CTO): Procurement also wants fallback controls — if a region loses capacity we need automated fallback to a smaller model to keep throughput.
00:09:48 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): That's built into the routing policies — you can set model-fallback chains and automatic downgrade thresholds. We'll demo that in the pilot.
00:09:58 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): Any known gotchas with cache-handoff?
00:10:02 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): A couple: 1) Cold-to-warm transition cost spike during initial onboarding, 2) Cache inconsistency if you have concurrent writes to the same prefix (rare for read-heavy chat), 3) Tail variance if using centralized KV under heavy network congestion.
00:10:17 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): For our workload mostly read, occasional updates to profile prefixes, sounds acceptable.
00:10:22 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Ok quick demo of the routing policy UI — you can set rules like "if latency > 120ms, route to dedicated model pool" or "if tokens-per-minute > threshold, enable adaptive batching."
00:10:38 Speaker 3: [background noise]
00:10:44 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Also note prefetch heuristics — you can set lookahead depth and prefetch TTLs. For example, prefetch top-k likely prefixes when session opens. We have an ML-based predictor but you can seed it with your heuristics.
00:10:59 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): How invasive is changing our client to support prefetch? We want minimal client changes.
00:11:05 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Minimal — a small SDK call when session opens to request prefetch keys; SDK returns a small token header to attach to subsequent requests. We have existing clients for node/python.
00:11:17 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): One more on cost model: what about infra costs for Redis? If we centralize KV we pay extra ops.
00:11:24 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Yes, we included Redis infra ops as a separate line item; often the infra cost is <5% of token spend for moderate traffic, but for ultra-high RPS it can grow — we'll add concrete numbers for your projected RPS.
00:11:38 Priya Singh (SpectralAI CTO): Can we get a quick sensitivity table in the spreadsheet for Redis cost per RPS?
00:11:44 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Yep that's part of the next deliverable.
00:11:48 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): Ok, procurement will also ask about compliance docs — SOC2, ISO, data residency.
00:11:54 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): I'll attach the SOC2 summary and our regional hosting map. For Private deployments we can ship the on-prem package and KMS connectors.
00:12:03 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): Let's talk about measuring the warm cache hit rate — what's realistic?
00:12:09 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Hit rate depends on repeat rate and TTL. With your sample 30% repeatable prefix rate and 10min TTL we simulated a warm hit rate of ~65% on peak after warmup; with handoff patterns it rose to ~78% because cross-session reuse improved.
00:12:26 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): That's promising. How long to warm?
00:12:29 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Warm time varies — cold to 50% hit rate in 12–30 minutes for typical spikes, less with prefetch on session open.
00:12:38 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): We'll instrument the pilot to capture warm-up curves.
00:12:42 Speaker 1: [crosstalk: yeah okay mmhm]
00:12:48 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): Failure modes — what if a worker crashes and we lose local GPU cache?
00:12:52 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Local cache is ephemeral; design for rehydration from central KV. Also set up TTLs and fallback to small model to avoid retries.
00:13:01 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): Can you produce a short runbook for ops to handle cache misses and evictions?
00:13:06 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Yes we'll include an ops runbook and alert playbooks.
00:13:10 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Going to the end: quick recap of deliverables and timeline.
00:13:14 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): 1) Ryan to send cost-model spreadsheet + initial Dedicated quote (by 2026-06-04).
00:13:20 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): 2) Maya to share SOC2 summary + Private deployment KMS notes (by 2026-06-05).
00:13:26 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): 3) Team to schedule 24h Dedicated pilot (target week of 2026-06-15).
00:13:32 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): Sounds good. Any blockers for pilot?
00:13:36 Priya Singh (SpectralAI CTO): We need NDA addendum for infra access — procurement will send that.
00:13:41 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): We'll coordinate with legal.
00:13:44 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): One last question on metrics: can we get token-level cost breakdown per route?
00:13:48 Maya Patel (Redwood SE): Yes, the console provides token-level breakdowns per model/route, and you can export.
00:13:55 Liam Brooks (Redwood CSM): We'll also set up a daily digest during the pilot so you can watch warmup and cost changes.
00:14:02 Speaker 2 (SpectralAI): [unintelligible comment]
00:14:08 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Great — if there are no other questions we'll wrap and I'll follow up with the sheet and quote.
00:14:14 Priya Singh (SpectralAI CTO): Thanks everyone.
00:14:16 Elena Ruiz (SpectralAI): Thanks, appreciate it.
00:14:18 Tom Bauer (SpectralAI): Thanks.
00:14:22 Ryan Chen (Redwood AE): Thanks all, we'll send notes.
00:14:27 [meeting end — recording continues for a few seconds]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (we sometimes saw "KV cahce" or "Redwood Optima" in auto-sub) — cleaned minimally above. The full console demo included live edits to the cost-sheet; we referenced "cost-model-sandbox.xlsx" (to be delivered).
